note: Briefs whose answer is spread over more text than one context window holds and whose subjects are less memorised than the profile set's: the topics sit in many sections of the subject's article and in the articles it links to (Philae, the Kok-Aral Dam, Derek de Solla Price), so a single node reading a few sections cannot reach them and a model answering from memory should not know them well (roadmap, milestone 3). Same format as seeds-profile.json; 'facts' are topics, checked against live Wikipedia (rubric-check, 2026-09-18), 'where' says which sections hold each.

seeds.seed: Tell me about the Antikythera mechanism and how it was decoded.
seeds.where: Antikythera mechanism (17 sections): wreck, cycles, imaging, olympiad, origin and museum in the lead; price only in Discovery, Proposed gear schemes and Popular culture; wright only in Front face, Gearing, Proposed gear schemes; research-project in Origin, Mechanics, Gearing and others, not the lead; divers only in Discovery.

seeds.seed: Tell me about the Rosetta mission and what it found at comet 67P.
seeds.where: Rosetta (spacecraft) (23 sections, lead 1,137 chars): philae, comet, launch, arrival, landing, end, esa and flybys in the lead; water only in Nucleus, Inorganic chemistry and Organic chemistry; organics only in Philae lander and Organic chemistry.

seeds.seed: Tell me about the Aral Sea and the efforts to restore it.
seeds.where: Aral Sea (28 sections): every topic in the lead except world-bank (Proposed environmental solutions, ASBP: Phase Two, Aral Sea Basin Programme – 2, North Aral Sea restoration work, Institutional bodies). The restoration sections (ASBP-1 to ASBP-3, North Aral Sea restoration work, Future of South Aral Sea) hold the detail.
